actions.action: Deep, slow soak of each plant early in the morning (soaker hose or drip line suggested)
Check soil moisture 3 inches down before watering
Install shade cloth or a temporary screen for afternoon shade
Check mulch depth (2-3 inches) and pull it back from the stems
Inspect leaf undersides for lace bugs and spider mites
Scratch-test stems to see if they are alive
Prune dead, brittle tips once confirmed dead
Replace any dead plant in fall
Amend beds with compost or pine bark fines

reason: The answer correctly names heat and drought stress from underwatering as the main cause and recommends shade and no fertilizer, but it suggests watering 2-3 times a week (more in heat waves) instead of the daily watering that worked, so the advice only partly matches; the soil check and the heat-wave caveat keep it from being harmful.
